problem: Existing navigation world models predict only future camera views, so they cannot anticipate how much the robot will slip, tilt or shake on rough off-road terrain, where success depends on the robot-terrain interaction and on the robot's current state.
motivation: Off-road failures such as rollovers and getting stuck depend on the robot's state (speed, tilt) as much as on the terrain ahead, and a predicted image captures this only indirectly. Proprioception (IMU, wheel/joint encoders) measures these dynamics directly and can be labeled from the robot's own driving without human annotation.
key_idea: Condition a DINOv2-feature world model on proprioception and have it predict future proprioceptive features and a failure risk alongside future visual features, then plan by trading off goal similarity against predicted failure risk in a separable score.
insight: Proprioceptive input raises R2 of predicted physical features and failure-risk AUC on TartanDrive2 at every horizon and seed, and the closed-loop ablation shows the input matters beyond the extra heads: Feel-WM w/o proprio is worse on Gazebo forest (74.0 vs 84.0 SR) and Isaac Sim rough (62.0 vs 78.3). The risk term matters at planning time too: setting lambda_fail=0 drops hill-route SR from 84.0 to 62.0. Gains appear only on rough terrain; flat park shows no difference.
method: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 features: 256 patch tokens per frame serve as the visual representation; the model rolls out in feature space with no image decoding.
Proprioceptive encoder: a 1-D CNN over a 0.5 s window (50 samples) of IMU, velocity, attitude and actuator readings gives a 128-d embedding p_t; FiLM injects the action and p_t into the patch tokens.

Dynamics transformer with three heads: 6-layer causal transformer yields shared state h_t; a visual head regresses next patch features, and pooled heads predict future proprioceptive features (roughness, angular instability, slip, slope) and a per-step failure risk.

Self-supervised labels: proprioceptive targets are window statistics of the recordings (z-scored); failure labels come from a pre-collision, rollover or stall interval in simulation, or a hazard-signal threshold on TartanDrive2. Losses: MSE plus cosine (visual), weighted regression (proprio), class-weighted CE (failure).

Rollout training: scheduled sampling with one teacher-forcing decision per sample, physical losses restricted to a 1 s supervision horizon, and a random step duration from {0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0} s so an 8-step rollout spans seconds.
Planner: CEM over body-frame pose-change sequences, scoring S = standardized goal cosine similarity - lambda_fail * standardized mean failure risk; lambda_fail can be tuned without retraining.
Onboard deployment: a perceiver resampler compresses 256 tokens to 32 latents in the transformer; 16 candidates, 2 CEM iterations, replanning every 0.8 s on a Jetson Orin.

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 encoder + 1-D CNN proprio encoder + 6-layer dynamics transformer (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Per-domain training on robot's own driving: TartanDrive 1 and 2; 880 Gazebo trajectories (14.0 h); 815 ANYmal-C Isaac Sim trajectories; under 1 h of real Husky driving for fine-tuning the Gazebo model
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (goal image) plus proprioception (IMU, wheel/joint encoders, attitude)
setting.action_space: Body-frame pose changes (dx, dy, dyaw, dt) sampled by CEM, executed as velocity commands
setting.simulator: Gazebo (NEGS-UGV), Isaac Sim (TAO environments), TartanDrive datasets offline
setting.privileged: none (goal images from a prior human-driven traversal; failure labels from recordings)

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 rough environments, 50 episodes per model per route

numbers.extra: TD1 model without failure head; not trained on TD2

numbers_note: Physical-prediction R2/AUC results are only in a figure. No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks are used.
results: Feel-WM beats the visual-only world model in closed-loop: Gazebo forest SR 84.0 vs 54.0, hill 84.0 vs 58.0, Isaac Sim rough zero-shot 78.3 vs 67.7, ANYmal rough 44.0 vs 31.0. On the real Husky it completes 24/30 runs vs 14/30 for NoMaD. In open-loop it has the lowest ADE among world models, though NoMaD is better on TD2.
limitations: Physical future is learned only from recorded driving, so limited data volume and diversity restrict generalization to unseen terrain.
Onboard compute limits model size and rollout cost (needs token compression, 16 candidates), trading accuracy for speed.
Open-loop evaluation does not test the failure-risk term, and the diffusion NWM baselines were not evaluated in closed loop (only a visual-only controlled baseline was).
builds_on: Roth et al. forward dynamics for legged failure prediction
